summary.text: Son of Bellerophon and father of Glaucus (`glaucus-lycian`), captain of the Lycians beside Sarpedon — distinct from Hippolochus son of Antimachus (`hippolochus-antimachid`), whom Agamemnon slew in *Iliad* 11.

story.text: When Hippolochus sent his son to Troy, he charged him always to be bravest and leave a good report of the race of his fathers, that he might not shame his lineage — men of Ephyra and Lycia who traced their line through Bellerophon.
Homer sets Glaucus, son of Hippolochus, among the Lycian leaders who smote Iphinous in the fierce conflict and followed Sarpedon when the allies stormed the wall.
